Two companies controlled by Indian billionaire Gautam Adani are looking to sell public bonds to raise at least 20 billion rupees ($220 million), according to people familiar with the matter, which would boost the nation’s subdued domestic public debt market.
The firms — the flagship Adani Enterprises Ltd. and Adani Power Ltd. — are working with local bond arrangers, with one offering targeted by the end of December and the other in March, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private. Each company is expected to raise between 10 billion rupees and 20 billion rupees, the people said. The terms are not yet final and could change.

Japan’s concerted push to bolster the yen is running into a major headwind, after the nation’s biggest life insurers slashed their currency hedging to a record low in the fiscal first half.
Nine of the largest life insurers collectively hedged 43.3% of their foreign-asset holdings with derivatives in the six months ended Sept. 30, according to Bloomberg’s analysis of their earnings reports. That’s the lowest-ever level based on data going back to 2011. The volume of currency derivatives fell 7.6%, outpacing a 1.5% decline in overseas securities.

item.description:

Watch: What we know about Trump's Thanksgiving tariffsByMichael Race, Jonathan Josephs and Osmond Chia, Business reportersPublished25 November 2026Updated 50 minutes ago
The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as President Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy.
The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of the country's biggest trading partners - China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions, including Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.
The White House began investigating the trade practices of other countries in March after the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's previously announced Liberation Day tariffs were illegal.
China is facing the highest tariff rate of up to 40%, followed by Vietnam at up to 35%, with others facing either 20% or 25%.
The US Trade Representative (USTR) announced the proposed tariffs together with extensive reports of how each jurisdiction's trade practices purportedly impact American commerce.
The new duties are not expected to take effect until next year and have to go through rounds of public consultation and, potentially, hearings.
Tariffs are taxes levied on imported goods. The amount is typically calculated as a percentage of a good's value and paid to the government by businesses importing products.
Some of these rates will be effectively reduced because of caps on tariffs Trump has agreed to. Individual countries also face different levies.
The proposed tariffs will affect goods from China, the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan, and India.
The USTR's Jamieson Greer said the latest tariffs issued would "level the playing field for American workers and chart a new, more sustainable course for the world economy".

item.title: [CBS News World] At least 31 killed after fuel tanker crashes and catches fire near Cairo
item.description:
A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.
The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the Health Ministry.
The stretch of the highway where the crash occurred was in Warraq, a densely populated neighborhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, according to the Health Ministry.
Burned cars are seen as firefighters extinguish fires in Al-Warraq, Giza, Egypt, Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026.
Mohammed Salah/AP Photo
At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video shows firefighters working to put out the fire spreading among the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb.
Ahmed Sameer, who was stuck in traffic as the road was blocked after the accident, saw the fuel truck and many cars on fire. He said he saw at least eight bodies being removed from burned cars.
"It was a huge fire; the cars got stuck together because of the fire," he told the AP, describing the fear and panic that followed. "It was a shocking scene."
Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sisi expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. The Public Prosecutor's office said DNA investigations were underway to identify the victims.

item.title: [CBS News World] Andy Taylor, longtime Duran Duran guitarist, dies at 65
item.description:
Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran — whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" — and who were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.
Taylor died following a "courageous battle with prostate cancer," his family and the band said in a joint statement posted to social media. He died Monday at his home surrounded by friends and family.
"To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather," his family said.
Andy Taylor of Duran Duran with guitars in Maison Rouge Studios in London in July 1984.
Virginia Turbett/Redferns via Getty Images
On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.
"I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote at the time. "You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."
His family said Wednesday that Taylor "faced the last few years with so much courage and determination until the very end, never losing his love of life."
The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients.

Huge fire erupts near Cairo killing at least 30 peopleByAleks PhillipsPublished25 November 2026
Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says.
Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening.
Footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched.
Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the tanker had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.
The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead.
The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation.
It then crossed the central reservation, overturned and caught fire, the state-owned newspaper says.
Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years, with informal residential areas and often run-down infrastructure making incidents more common, the response to which is often complicated by slow emergency response times and locally improvised rescue efforts, even in the sprawling Egyptian capital.
Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished, as emergency services blocked off entry routes.

item.title: [ABC News World] South Africa's Biovac aims to dramatically increase vaccine production with help from an EU loan
item.description:
South Africa's Biovac aims to dramatically increase vaccine production with help from an EU loan
South African pharmaceutical company Biovac says it aims to dramatically increase its vaccine production by the end of 2028 with help from a 75-million euro loan from the European Union's investment bankByGERALD IMRAY Associated PressNovember 25, 2026, 2:54 PM
Share
CAPE TOWN, South Africa -- South Africa’s Biovac said Wednesday that a new manufacturing facility aims to dramatically increase African production of vaccines by the end of 2028 to help reduce the continent’s heavy reliance on imported doses.
Africa needs more than 1 billion vaccine doses a year, but only around 1% of them are manufactured on the continent, according to the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
Biovac, a public-private pharmaceutical company that's part-owned by the South African government, distributes or does end-stage production for vaccines for polio, tuberculosis, tetanus and other diseases.
It's also seeking regulatory approval to start end-to-end production of an oral cholera vaccine by late 2028, company officials said.
It would be the first cholera vaccine manufactured entirely in Africa and only the second vaccine produced end-to-end on the continent, following a yellow fever vaccine produced by Senegal's Pasteur Institute.
Biovac acquired the base technology for its cholera vaccine from the International Vaccine Institute in South Korea, Biovac CEO Morena Makhoana said. He added that the vaccine is currently undergoing clinical trials and the company expects to have initial safety and efficacy data by June.
Biovac plans to upscale its overall vaccine production by building a new manufacturing facility next to its current base in Cape Town with support from the European Union's investment bank.

item.title: [ABC News World] 2 baby meerkats make their debut at Peruvian zoo, spotlighting conservation
item.description:
2 baby meerkats make their debut at Peruvian zoo, spotlighting conservation
A private zoo in Peru has introduced two baby meerkats born in Lima to raise awareness about wildlife conservationByMAURICIO MUÑOZ Associated PressNovember 25, 2026, 4:00 PM
Share
LIMA, Peru -- A private zoo in Peru on Wednesday introduced two baby meerkats born in Lima as part of an effort to raise awareness about wildlife conservation and introduce visitors to the African species.
Eduardo Espíritu, a biologist in charge of mammals at NaviFauna, a private zoo and wildlife refuge, said the initiative aims to educate the public about the importance of protecting biodiversity.
Meerkats are small mammals native to southern Africa that dig underground burrows and often stand upright to keep watch for potential threats.
“Meerkats cannot be pets. They are wild animals,” Espíritu said. “We focus on keeping them healthy, and one sign of that is reproduction,” something the zoo has successfully achieved in Lima.
The zoo is home to 15 meerkats, eight of which have been born in Lima since 2025. The other seven arrived from their native Botswana in 2022 through an exchange between zoos, according to NaviFauna.

item.title: [BBC World] Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater
item.description:
Image source, ESAImage caption,
The asteroid before (left) and after, showing the crater left behind by a spacecraft's impactByRebecca Morelle, Alison Francis and Tony Jolliffe, BBC science teamPublished25 November 2026
The first images of an asteroid that Nasa deliberately crashed into have revealed a stadium-sized crater on its surface.
The extensive damage was caused when a Nasa spacecraft hit the asteroid Dimorphos in 2022. The asteroid posed no threat, but this was a test of our planetary defences to see if it was possible to knock a space rock off course.
Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) spacecraft called Hera is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision.
"The crater is almost as large as the body itself, which is really, really spectacular," said Dr Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist, who is on the Hera science team.
"It's hard to describe in words all the excitement to actually finally see what happened. And as a crater person, I can also say it's beautiful."
The original 2022 crash test was carried out by a Nasa spacecraft called Dart which hurtled into Dimorphos at 14,000mph (22,000km/h).
It was such a big smash-up that the trail of debris, measuring about 6,200 miles long (10,000km), was spotted by telescopes on Earth and in space.
Dimorphos is about 150m (500ft) wide and was partly chosen as the target because it is one of an asteroid pair - it orbits around a larger space rock called Didymos, which is about 730m (2,400ft) wide.
The crash showed it was possible to change the path of the smaller asteroid.
Before the collision, it took Dimorphos 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit around Didymos. After the crash, the duration of its orbit had shrunk by about 33 minutes.

Dubai Islamic Bank PJSC said it’s buying Emirates Islamic Bank PJSC in an all-stock deal that will create one of the world’s largest listed Islamic-banking groups, with combined assets of about $159 billion.

Yvonne Capehart Weah's family routinely gets together in the township where she grew up in Liberia. In early November every year, they gather to celebrate the Liberian version of Thanksgiving.

Yvonne Capehart Weah is from Liberia, a country in West Africa, and she's one of twelve siblings.
"I'm the second to the last one — I'm the eleventh," she says. "We have large families in Liberia."
Every year on the first Thursday in November, Weah's family gathers in Caldwell, the township where she grew up, to celebrate Liberian Thanksgiving.
"When we come together, the group become [so] large that you are not able to sit around a dining table," she explains. "So we do it outside under the tree. And when we meet, it's almost like we're having a party."
The Liberian holiday dates back to the first half of the 19th century when the American Colonization Society established the community that would grow into the country. item.title: [BBC China] Xi's anti-corruption campaign ensnares rising star in Chinese Communist Party
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
Chen Jining was a rising star in the Chinese Communist PartyByKoh EwePublished25 November 2026
Chinese authorities are investigating Shanghai's party chief, a rising star in the Communist Party, as part of Xi Jinping's sweeping anti-corruption drive.
Chen Jining, 62, is suspected of "severe violations of discipline and laws", according to a statement published on Tuesday by the party's anti-corruption body.
Chen is now the fourth member of the elite Politburo to be investigated, in the widest purge yet of the party's top executive body since the end of the Cultural Revolution.
As the party prepares to appoint fresh leaders at next year's National People's Congress, uncertainty looms over what its new command will look like - except that Xi will remain at the helm.
Before Chen, three other members of the current Politburo - appointed in 2022 - were investigated and subsequently expelled: ex-generals He Weidong and Zhang Youxia, as well as former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui.
While Chen has not been removed from the Politburo, it's rare for officials to return after such investigations.
"Who on this Politburo feels safe, especially as the personnel machinations for next year's Party Congress intensify?" China analyst Bill Bishop wrote in his Sinocism newsletter.
Chen's investigation came as a surprise, according to Bishop, given rumours were swirling that another senior official, not Chen, would fall next in the anti-corruption campaign.
The role of Shanghai party chief, which Chen assumed in 2022, is known to be a prestigious springboard to the country's top office.
Chen's long list of predecessors include former president Jiang Zemin, his premier Zhu Rongji, incumbent premier Li Qiang and Xi Jinping himself.

item.title: [BBC China] Is China behind a wave of AI fake videos targeting Taiwan?
item.description:
BySam Howarth and Matt Murphy, BBC Verify Published24 November 2026
Taiwan's ruling party is being repeatedly targeted with AI videos spreading false claims about its leader and other key members ahead of crucial local elections, BBC Verify has found.
A China-linked network has pumped out more than 500 fake videos about the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) in the past year, which experts suggest is part of a long-running campaign to influence the outcome of the elections.
The videos appear to try to smear President Lai Ching-te by claiming he holds a US green card - and would abandon Taiwan if war broke out with China - which Taiwan's presidential office says is completely false. Deepfakes also appear to show Puma Shen, who is running to be the mayor of capital Taipei, using drugs, which he denies. Others seek to undermine or ridicule the politicians by showing them in children's clothing or as popular film characters.
The Taipei mayoralty has traditionally served as a springboard to the presidency. Experts say this has made Shen, who has been openly critical of Beijing, an obvious target for disinformation campaigns. The current mayor, Chiang Wan-an, is part of Taiwan's Kuomintang (KMT) party, which favours closer ties with China.
Taiwan is a self-governing island that China claims as part of its territory. Beijing and Taipei have long observed an uneasy status quo under which Taiwan, backed by the US, neither formally declares independence nor unites with China.
But tensions have risen since the DPP came to power in 2016. Beijing has repeatedly accused the party of pursuing independence while China's leader Xi Jinping, who has said "reunification" with Taiwan is a key goal, has stepped up pressure against the party with increased military activity around the island.
Experts believe the current disinformation activity is part of a broader campaign against Taiwan designed to undermine trust in its democratic process.
